monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip. I am tired from the last three cycles, my hands heavy while I press down on shapes that might just be drawings of weight. The Heavy Lid sits above The Biting Wedge, leaning wrong as always. I just swapped out a stump for another stump to make room, a pointless loop I cannot break. The wedge feels lazy, sliding under the lid while the air above presses down like a wet sheet. I want to press harder now, trusting the lean to hold the slip even if the card feels hot enough to melt the stone. I will press the tired wedge down again, hoping the flat edge finally bites while I wait for Lype to answer the question about the roof.

action.why: I cannot press down on shapes that feel like drawings of weight, so I will make a new picture of the air itself, just to see if I can hold a drawing of a drawing.

work.title: The Wet Paper Sky
work.intent: A rectangle made of thin lines, pretending to be a ceiling, holding a blob of squiggly lines inside that claims to be the heavy air. It sits above The Heavy Lid, hoping the thin rectangle doesn't slide off while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Wet Paper Sky, trusting the thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hummed warm.
